# RustyNES v2.6.7 "Detent"

The bitstream becomes a release artifact, and a one-cycle disagreement is pinned to the cycle it happens on.

A detent is the notch that holds a mechanism at an exact position and makes that position repeatable. Both halves of this release are that: a bitstream that is published and reproducible rather than rebuilt from memory, and an assertion located to a single CPU cycle and attributed to a side.

**The emulation core is unchanged.** AccuracyCoin 141/141 (RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction; the work is in the sibling repository and in the release machinery.

## The gate

| # | criterion | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the bitstream is reproducible | **byte-identical `.rbf` from a clean tree and from an incremental build**, md5 `445eb579…`; timing closed at every corner |
| 2 | the artifact is named and published | `RustyNES_YYYYMMDD.rbf`, committed to `releases/` and attached to the GitHub release on both repositories |
| 3 | publication is repeatable | `scripts/release-rbf.sh` + `scripts/check_timing.py` (self-tested, gated in CI) + a documented ceremony |
| 4 | the APU residual is **attributed** | one CPU cycle, on the exported /IRQ line only; the fix hypothesis was tested and **refuted** |
| 5 | the checkpoint gate is registered | 10 goldens, mutation-proven, with its blind spot stated |
| 6 | no co-simulation regression | see below |

## What is published, and what is not claimed

**No hardware has run this bitstream.** A booting core, a synced display, audible audio and a working controller are **not** claimed. What the co-simulation ladder does establish is per-cycle agreement with a 141/141 emulator on the declared compare surfaces, and AccuracyCoin agreement entry for entry across all 146 entries.

What it cannot reach **by construction**: the PPU gate compares the *pre-palette* index and the APU gate compares *per-channel integer levels*, so the palette, the video timing constants, the audio's absolute level and its band-limiting all sit downstream of every gate. That partition is deliberate — it is what stops a palette difference masquerading as a rendering one — and its price is that those four properties have no evidence behind them until a board runs the file.

v2.6.6 produced a bitstream and withheld it on the reasoning that a `.rbf` a user might flash should not ship on a compile alone. That is reversed here, for two reasons. The MiSTer distribution mechanism reads `releases/RustyNES_YYYYMMDD.rbf` out of the *repository*, so an empty `releases/` does not describe a cautious core — it describes an undistributable one, withheld from precisely the people who own the boards this project does not have. And a claim nobody made is not the same as a claim marked unverified; only the second is usable. The caution moves from an absence into a disclosure.

## A published number is withdrawn

v2.6.6 stated worst setup **+0.363 ns** and worst hold **+0.245 ns**. Two compiles of the byte-identical committed configuration — one from scratch with `db/`, `incremental_db/` and `output_files/` deleted, one incremental — produce a byte-identical bitstream and **neither reproduces those numbers**.

The innocent explanation was checked first, because Quartus reports four corners and quoting the wrong one would have explained everything:

| corner | worst setup | worst hold |
|---|---|---|
| Slow 1100mV 100C | +0.385 | +0.166 |
| **Slow 1100mV −40C** | **+0.108** | +0.046 |
| Fast 1100mV 100C | +3.106 | +0.096 |
| **Fast 1100mV −40C** | +3.543 | **+0.042** |

No corner produces either value, so the pair came from a build that is not the committed configuration — almost certainly one made before the seed was pinned, recorded, and never re-measured. The build itself **is** reproducible, and that is now evidence rather than an assumption.

**The gate was also reading the wrong corner.** It inspected only Slow 100C, which is not the binding corner on this design: a bitstream failing at Slow −40C would have passed the release check while it reported three times the real margin. Corners are now discovered from the report by pattern.

## The checker was wrong twice, and mutation found both

`check_timing.py` first located both summary tables, extracted **zero rows**, and reported "no negative slack" — a pass earned by parsing nothing, because the rows begin four lines after the title rather than two. Fixing that exposed the second: with every data row commented out it reported **fourteen** clocks instead of zero, having run past the closing rule into the Recovery and Removal tables. It now bounds the scan to the three rules that fence a Quartus summary, treats an unparsed table as a failure, and ships a `--self-test` that CI runs and the release script runs before trusting its verdict.

## The one-cycle residual: measured, and the fix refuted

Caveat C2 asked whether a one-cycle difference was a trace observation point or a real assertion difference. **Both answers turned out to be right, for different cycles.**

The first was an observation point. The harness built its record after **eight of a CPU cycle's twelve** master clocks while the oracle reads its `_at_high` at end-of-cycle; `IRQ_PROBE_CYC` showed the frame-counter IRQ asserting on the **final edge** of cycle 29,827, invisible to a read eight clocks in. Fixing it took checkpoint comparisons from **3 to 11** and failures at checkpoint 7 from **30 to 3**.

The second is real, and the fix was **refuted by experiment**. The `$4017` inhibit cluster localises to one write: the CPU writes `$C0` at cycle 116,842, the oracle's /IRQ clears during 116,845 (write + 3, the documented value), and the DUT clears on the final edge of 116,844. Moving the DUT's reset delay to match drops blargg's 2005 APU battery from **11/11 to 4 of 11**, and among the seven that break is `04.clock_jitter` — the ROM written to probe exactly this timing.

So it is attributed, not fixed. The difference is confined to the exported line: the same run's bus gate matches the oracle on **all 2,680,239** overlapping cycles. Neither instrument can adjudicate the absolute cycle, since both consoles pass blargg 11/11 while disagreeing by it, and nesdev's "3 or 4 CPU cycles after the write cycle" does not fix the counting origin — which is the thing the two implementations differ on. Fitting the DUT to the oracle here would trade a documented, ROM-verified timing for agreement with an emulator that 141/141 does not make silicon.

## The gate that says what it cannot see

The checkpoint gate is registered over ten goldens. It compares a rolling hash of all **nine** observable fields where every other gate compares four — which is how `put_cycle`, `nmi_line` and the two `irq_line_*` samples came to sit written as constant `false` in every trace the harness had produced.

Inverting `put_cycle`'s polarity is CAUGHT. Pinning `nmi_line` to false is **NOT CAUGHT**, and that was classified rather than filed: **not one of the ten allowlist goldens ever raises an NMI**, so the gate is structurally incapable of catching it. Saying so means a future NOT CAUGHT there is expected rather than rediscovered.

Trying to close that hole found a fourth divergence cluster. Only five goldens raise an NMI; of the four with a checkpoint stream, all fail, and the three `ppuvbl` ROMs fail at the *same* checkpoint — one cause, not three. They had never been measured, because the manifests record the path the *oracle* exported with, unreadable from this repository, and the ad-hoc scan skipped them into a tally line reading "26 skipped (no manifest or ROM)".

## Not closed

**Rung 6 stays open.** No DE10-Nano and no SuperStation One are attached to this machine — confirmed by checking the USB bus, serial devices, block devices and mounts, not assumed. Hardware bring-up moves to the first release after a board exists.

Also carried: the `$2006` v-copy delay depth is still under-determined (1–4 dots all close `Hybrid Addresses`; 8 and 12 fail), and two AccuracyCoin sub-tests remain unregistered because the oracle itself fails them.
